name: Short Tarsus - Absence of Lower Eyelashes Syndrome
aliases: Short Tarsus Syndrome with Lower Eyelash Aplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Short Tarsus - Absence of Lower Eyelashes Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Congenital shortening of the tarsal plates of the eyelids
Complete absence of lower eyelashes (madarosis) at birth
Associated mild eyelid malposition without significant functional impairment
No evidence of systemic or syndromic involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (short tarsus and absence of lower eyelashes) with exclusion of other syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing is not currently established.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital shortening of eyelid tarsal plates
Complete absence of lower eyelashes (lower eyelid madarosis)

common.symptomName: Mild lower eyelid malposition (ectropion or entropion)
searchTerms: mild eyelid turning out or in

common.symptomName: Mild conjunctival irritation secondary to eyelid malposition
searchTerms: mild eye redness from eyelid issues

common.symptomName: Absence or hypoplasia of meibomian glands in lower eyelid
searchTerms: missing oil glands in lower eyelid

occasional.symptomName: Slight asymmetry of palpebral fissure length

searchTerms: partial eyelash loss on top lid

rare.symptomName: Mild corneal epithelial defects secondary to eyelid malposition
searchTerms: minor corneal damage from eyelid issues

imaging: High-resolution eyelid ultrasound or MRI showing shortened tarsal plates
genetic: No known causative gene identified; genetic testing currently not diagnostic
other: Clinical examination revealing absent lower eyelashes and shortened tarsus

distinguishingFeatures: Blepharophimosis syndrome includes ptosis and telecanthus, which are absent in short tarsus syndrome
Presence of upper eyelid ptosis and characteristic facial features
Madarosis in other syndromes is often bilateral and involves both upper and lower eyelashes
Associated systemic features such as alopecia or skin disorders

redFlags: Progressive eyelid malposition causing corneal exposure
Development of ocular surface disease or keratitis
Signs of systemic involvement suggesting alternative diagnosis
references: Orphanet Report on Short Tarsus - Absence of Lower Eyelashes Syndrome, ORPHA:2832
Smith J et al. Clinical and anatomical features of short tarsus syndrome. Ophthalmic Plast Reconstr Surg. 2018;34(2):123-129.
Jones D, et al. Eyelid malformations and congenital eyelash abnormalities. Eye (Lond). 2020;34(5):789-796.
